newsitem.title: CANADA: Fletcher Canada, unions consolidate talks.
newsitem.headline: Fletcher Canada, unions consolidate talks.

text.p: Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd said on Friday that contract negotiations with its unions would be consolidated into one set of talks starting next week.
The company was previously negotiating separately with local unions at the pulp and paper company's three mills, a company spokeswoman said.

But since many local issues had been "dropped or resolved," the two sides agreed to a single set of talks, she said. "This means there will be a central forum to negotiate major issues that apply to all our operations," she said.
She declined to specify those issues or discuss the significance of the step. "As long as we're talking, we're making progress," she said.
Fletcher and its two unions -- the Communications, Energy and Paperworkers union and the Pulp, Paper and Woodworkers of Canada union -- have been bargaining since March.
They are discussing a new accord to replace a contract that expired on April 30.
The company and unions agreed not to comment on the talks publicly. But some industry sources have said progress was slow.

Fletcher was chosen as the target for pattern bargaining. The unions expect to replicate any contract agreed on with Fletcher at other pulp and paper companies employing 14,000 workers in British Columbia.
Fletcher, the province's biggest producer of pulp and paper, was hit by six-week strike in late 1994 and early 1995 when it bargained its last contract.
